docs.title: Stutastic Planner
docs.text: Stutastic Planner keeps your semester in one place: your timetable, assignments, tests, revision, grades, attendance and focus time. It works offline, on your device first. Sign in if you want it synced across your phone, tablet, computer and the web.

docs.title: New here?
docs.text:
1. Set up your semester. A few short steps: your university, your semester's dates, your subjects and your classes. If your university is supported, your timetable can come straight from its student portal.
  2. Learn your way around. Where everything is on a phone, a tablet and a computer, plus keyboard shortcuts.
  3. Decide about an account. You don't need one. See Guest mode vs. an account.

docs.title: Common tasks
docs.text: I want to… Go to Add a class, or cancel or move one date of it Planner Bring my timetable in from my university Import from your university Track an assignment and how far along it is Tasks Plan revision for a test Study topics and Quizzes and exams Record marks and see my GPA Subjects and academics Know how many more classes I can miss Attendance Study in focused blocks Focus sessions Get reminded before class and about deadlines Reminders Mark a public holiday or add an event Agenda, events and holidays Keep a copy of everything, or move to a new device Export and import

docs.title: Where it runs
docs.text: iPhone and iPad, Android, Mac, Windows, Linux and the web. Most screens are the same everywhere; reminders, the Lock Screen timer and the tray differ by platform. See System requirements and the feature overview.

docs.title: Help
docs.text: Check the FAQ, or contact support. Read the Privacy Policy for what the app collects.

docs.title: Frequently asked questions
docs.text:
Does Stutastic Planner work offline? Yes. Planner changes are saved on your device. If you use an account, they sync when you are online. Guest records stay on that device. See Offline use and sync.

Do I need to create an account? No. Choose Not now, keep it on this device during setup to continue as a guest. Guest records do not sync. See Guest mode vs. an account.

How do I use my guest data on another device? Create an account from Settings → Account to sync your current planner data, or export a backup and restore it on the other device. See Export and Import.

Why are reminders unavailable in the web app? The web app does not schedule reminders. Use one of the apps, turn on Settings → Reminders, and allow notifications in your device settings. Reminders are stored on that device and do not need an account. See Reminders.

My reminders stopped. Reminders are scheduled two weeks ahead; open the app to schedule the next two weeks. Check that notifications are still allowed for Stutastic Planner in your device's settings. On Linux, Planner must be running.

How do I connect Google Calendar? Sign in to Stutastic Planner, then open Settings → Google Calendar and choose Connect Google Calendar. The app manages a dedicated calendar for its own planner items. See Settings.

How do I disconnect Google Calendar? Open Settings → Google Calendar and choose Disconnect. You can also delete your account without disconnecting first; account deletion attempts to remove the Calendar connection automatically. If that cleanup cannot be confirmed, deletion stops so you can retry.

Can I import a timetable? Yes, two ways, both from the ⋯ menu on the Planner. Import from your university signs in to a supported student portal and brings in your subjects and classes. Paste a timetable takes one class per line. See Bring in a timetable.

A class is cancelled this week. Do I delete it? No. Open the class and choose Cancel a date: only that date goes, and the rest of the term stays. Reschedule a date moves one date instead. For a public holiday that cancels every class, add a holiday.

My class alternates weeks. How do I add it? Set the semester's Week A anchor date, then set the class to repeat Every 2 weeks in Week A or Week B. See Alternating weeks.

Why does my GPA have a "~" in front? Some subjects in it don't have a final grade yet, so it's an estimate. See Grading scales and GPA.

How many more classes can I miss? Open the subject's Attendance tab, or check the Dashboard's Attendance warnings card. See Attendance.

Can I see the focus timer on my Lock Screen? On iPhone, yes: a running session shows on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island. On Android it shows as a notification. See Focus sessions.

Are there keyboard shortcuts? Yes, on any device with a keyboard. See Getting around.

Can I create a backup? Yes. In Settings → Your data, choose Export everything to save a JSON backup. See Export and Import.

How do I delete my account? Open Settings → Account and choose Delete my account. Export anything you want to keep first. The app also attempts to disconnect Google Calendar; if it cannot confirm cleanup, account deletion stops so you can retry. See Settings.

Is planner data used for advertising? The app does not include advertising. Firebase usage analytics is on by default and can be turned off for a device under Settings → Privacy. See the Privacy Policy.

How do I report a problem? Use the support tracker. Search existing issues first, then choose Report a bug. Include the app version, device and OS, and the steps that caused the problem. Choose Private if the report contains account or personal information. Do not upload passwords, sign-in codes, or private study records. See Support for details.

docs.title: Offline use and sync
docs.text: Stutastic Planner saves planner changes to a local database on your device first. You can use the planner while offline.

docs.title: Guest mode
docs.text: Guest planner records stay on the device and do not sync. Export a backup regularly if you need a second copy or plan to move to another device. Clearing app data or uninstalling the app can remove the local copy.

docs.title: Using an account
docs.text: When you are signed in and online, your planner records sync to your account. Changes made offline remain on the device and sync when the connection returns. Sign in to the same account on another device to access its synced records there.

docs.title: Internet connection
docs.text: Offline use does not require a connection for local planner actions. Sign-in, account creation, cross-device sync, and Google Calendar connection do require internet access.

docs.title: App and browser storage
docs.text: The native app keeps its local database in app storage. The web app uses browser storage. If you clear browser or app data, or uninstall the app, unsynced guest data may be lost. Use Export and Import to create a backup.

docs.title: Installing the web app
docs.text: You can use the web app in a browser or install it from the browser's install option when available. This is optional; iPhone and iPad also have a native app. Web reminders are not available, so use the native app if you want scheduled reminders from Stutastic Planner.

docs.title: Support
docs.text: Use the Stutastic Planner support tracker to search known issues, vote for one that affects you, or report a new bug or feature request. You don't need an account, and the team replies through the tracker.

docs.title: Before you report
docs.text:
• Check the FAQ and search the support tracker first — the issue may already be known and have a workaround.
  • Update to the latest version of the app and try again.
  • Note your app version from Settings → About, your device model, your operating system or browser version, and whether you use the web/PWA, iPhone/iPad, Android, or desktop app.
  • Write down the steps that led to the problem, what you expected to happen, and what actually happened.
  • Screenshots, recordings, or relevant log files help. Remove personal or study information you don't need to share.

docs.title: Report a bug or request a feature
docs.text:
1. Open support.danplace.tech/p/stu.
  2. Search for an existing issue and vote for it, or choose Report a bug.
  3. Fill in the area, summary, what happened, optional steps to reproduce, expected and actual results, how much it affects you, and your environment if it is relevant.
  4. Choose Public or Private. Public reports, their replies, and their attachments are visible to everyone. Use Private for account details, personal information, or anything you don't want public.
  5. Enter your name and email address. Your email is never shown publicly; it is used to send you a private link to follow the report and to email you when its status changes.
  6. Submit the report. Open the private link in the email to follow replies or add more detail. If you lose the email, use Email me my links to get a fresh private link for every report submitted from your address.

You can attach up to five files, up to 15 MB each: images, video, PDF, text, or log files. Don't upload passwords, sign-in codes, or private academic records.

docs.title: Follow-up and privacy
docs.text:
• The tracker is a separate service from your Stutastic Planner account. See the Privacy Policy for what it stores and how to ask for deletion.
  • If you can't sign in to delete your account, submit a Private report from the address on the account and ask us to delete it. Don't include your password.
  • For a privacy request about the app or the tracker, use a Private report as well.

For account, sync, calendar, or notification questions, the FAQ and the rest of this site may answer it without waiting for a reply.

docs.title: Export and import
docs.text: A backup is a single file with all your planner data: semesters, subjects, classes, tasks, tests, topics, attendance and focus history. Make one before you change devices, clear the app's data, or replace what you have. Guest data has no other copy.

docs.title: Export everything
docs.text:
1. Open Settings → Your data.
  2. Choose Export everything and save the file somewhere safe.

The backup is a dated JSON file. It works offline and in guest mode. It never contains your password or any kept university login, but it does contain your study records, so keep it private.

docs.title: Restore from a backup
docs.text:
1. Open Settings → Your data and choose Restore from a backup.
  2. Pick the file. Backups from this app and from the old web app both work.
  3. Choose how to apply it:
    • Merge keeps what you have and adds or updates what's in the file.
    • Replace deletes your current planner data first, then restores the file. It asks you to confirm, because it can't be undone.

Restoring brings back your planner data, not your sign-in. Sign in separately if you want it synced.

docs.title: Restore on a new device
docs.text:
On a fresh install you can restore before setting anything up:

  1. On the welcome screen, choose Restore a backup.
  2. Choose Choose a backup file and pick it. On iPhone and iPad, it can be in Files, iCloud Drive or On My iPhone.
  3. The app says how many records will be added; choose Restore.

Setup is then skipped and you land on your Dashboard as a guest, with everything from the backup. Create an account afterwards from Settings → Account if you want it synced.

Set up without a backup goes back to the normal setup.

docs.title: Move to another device
docs.text:
• With an account: sign in on the new device. Everything comes down from your account.
  • As a guest: export a backup, move the file to the new device (by AirDrop, email to yourself or a cloud drive), and restore it there. Or create an account on the old device first, then sign in on the new one.

docs.title: Import a timetable
docs.text: To add classes rather than a whole planner, use the Planner's menu: Import from your university or Paste a timetable.

docs.title: Privacy information
docs.text:
Read the Stutastic Planner Privacy Policy for what the app processes, when planner records sync, and how to control usage analytics and account data.

For privacy or support questions, use the support tracker and choose Private for anything personal. See Support for what to include in a report.

docs.title: Privacy Policy
docs.text:
Last updated: 21 November 2026

This Privacy Policy describes how Stutastic Planner, published by Danish Studio Production, handles information when you use the app and its support tracker. For privacy questions or requests, use the support tracker and choose Private for anything personal.

docs.title: Planner records
docs.text:
Planner records can include programme, semester, subject, class, event, task, quiz, result, study topic, focus-session, and preference information that you enter.

  • In guest mode, planner records stay in the app's local database on that device and are not synced to an account.
  • When you use a signed-in account, planner records are stored locally and synced through PowerSync and Supabase so you can use them on your other signed-in devices.
  • If you use the support tracker, we receive the information you submit there — see Support tracker. Please do not upload passwords, sign-in codes, or private academic records.

docs.title: Account information
docs.text: If you create or use an account, Firebase Authentication and your chosen sign-in provider process account information such as your email address, display name, and sign-in credentials. You can sign in with Google or email; Apple sign-in is available on Apple platforms. Stutastic Planner does not receive your Google or Apple account password.

docs.title: Usage analytics
docs.text: Firebase Analytics is enabled by default. It sends automatic app-usage events and an app-install identifier. Planner records are not sent through Analytics. You can turn off Usage analytics at Settings → Privacy. This setting is stored on each device and stops future Analytics collection from that device; it does not erase information already collected by Google.

docs.title: Reminders
docs.text: On supported native platforms, class and deadline reminders are scheduled locally on your device. The app creates and schedules reminders locally; it does not use push messaging for reminders. The operating system displays the notification text. You can turn reminders off in the app or manage notification permission in your device settings. Reminders are not available on the web.

docs.title: Google Calendar
docs.text: Google Calendar connection is optional and requires a signed-in Stutastic Planner account and your Google authorization. The app creates a dedicated calendar for its own classes, tasks, and quizzes. It does not access or manage your other Google calendars. A server-side authorization token is used to keep that calendar in sync. Choose Disconnect at Settings → Google Calendar to end the connection and ask Google to remove the Stutastic Planner calendar. Account deletion also attempts to disconnect Google Calendar and removes the server-side sync token and mapping. If that server-side cleanup cannot be confirmed, account deletion stops so you can retry. Google may leave the dedicated calendar in your Google Account if it cannot complete the removal; you can remove it from Google Calendar yourself.

docs.title: University timetable import
docs.text:
Importing from your university is optional. When you use it:

  • IIUM: the app signs in to i-Ma'luum directly from your device. Your student ID and password go only to IIUM's own sign-in page, over an encrypted connection, and are never sent to us. Your timetable and results are read on your device the same way.
  • Other universities: the app sends your chosen university, student ID and portal password over an encrypted connection to the Stutastic Planner import service. The service uses them only to sign in to your university's portal and return your timetable to the app. It doesn't store your password, student ID or timetable, and its logs are turned off.
  • To prevent misuse, the service counts sign-in attempts per network address and per student ID for about an hour. These counts are kept under one-way (SHA-256) hashes, never the address or ID itself. Requests must also carry a Firebase App Check token showing they come from the app.
  • Your university's portal receives your student ID and password, as when you sign in to it yourself. Its own privacy policy applies to that sign-in.
  • The app remembers your chosen university and student ID on your device so you don't retype them. Your password is not kept unless you choose Keep me signed in to refresh my timetable.
  • If you choose to stay signed in, your password is kept only on your device, in the operating system's secure storage. It's never synced to your account, sent to us for storage, or included in exports. The record of which semester follows which portal also stays on your device and isn't synced. Choose Forget my login at Settings → Your university to delete it; signing out or deleting your account also deletes it. This option isn't offered on the web.
  • The import service is free software under the GNU Affero General Public License. Its source code is available at github.com/Jerit3787/planner-connect.

docs.title: Support tracker
docs.text:
Bug reports, feature requests, votes, and replies are handled through the support tracker at support.danplace.tech. You can browse and search public issues without an account. Reporters do not need to sign in.

When you submit a report, you provide:

  • the app and area, a summary, what happened, optional steps to reproduce, expected and actual results, and the environment (for example, device and browser);
  • how much it affects you, and optionally up to five attachments (images, video, PDF, text, or log files, up to 15 MB each);
  • whether the report is Public (anyone can see, vote, and reply) or Private (only you and the team can see it);
  • your name and email address.

Your email address is never shown publicly. It is used to send you a private link to follow your report and to email you when its status changes. Email me my links at support.danplace.tech/links sends a fresh private link for every report submitted from your address.

The tracker stores reports, votes, replies, attachments, and the name and email you provide. Public reports and their attachments are visible to anyone; choose Private for account details, personal information, or anything you do not want public. Do not upload passwords, sign-in codes, or private academic records.

The tracker is hosted by Vercel. Support reports are a separate record from your Stutastic Planner account: deleting the account does not automatically delete them. We keep them for as long as needed to investigate the issue and keep a record of it. To ask us to delete a report or your contact details, reply on the private link emailed to you or submit a Private report.

docs.title: How information is used
docs.text:
Information is used to provide the planner, authenticate accounts, sync planner records across your devices, import and refresh your university timetable when you ask, maintain an optional Google Calendar connection, schedule local reminders, respond to support requests, and understand general app usage when Analytics is enabled.

Stutastic Planner does not include advertising and does not sell your personal information.

docs.title: Service providers
docs.text:
The app uses third-party services to provide its features. Those providers process information as described in their own policies:

  • Google and Firebase privacy information — account authentication and usage analytics. Google Calendar also receives the planner events you choose to sync.
  • PowerSync privacy policy — account data synchronization.
  • Supabase privacy policy — storage and services used for account data.
  • Apple privacy policy — if you choose Apple sign-in.
  • Cloudflare privacy policy — hosting for the university timetable import service.
  • Vercel privacy policy — hosting for the support tracker.

docs.title: Retention and deletion
docs.text:
Signed-in planner records remain associated with your account until you delete the account. To remove your Stutastic Planner account and synced planner records, choose Delete my account at Settings → Account. The app requires an internet connection to complete deletion of synced data. Account deletion also removes the server-side Google Calendar sync token and mapping. If the app cannot confirm that cleanup, it stops deletion so you can retry. The dedicated calendar is managed by Google and may remain in your Google Account if Google cannot complete its removal.

Support reports, votes, replies, attachments, and the name and email you provide are kept for as long as needed to investigate the issue and keep a record of it. You can ask us to delete a report or your contact details using the private link emailed to you or by submitting a Private report. Deleting your Stutastic Planner account does not automatically delete support reports.

Turning Analytics off stops future collection from that device. Information already collected by Firebase Analytics follows Google's retention settings. Service providers may retain copies in backups according to their own retention practices.

You can export planner records as a JSON file from Settings → Your data. The export contains planner records, not account credentials. Protect the file as you would any personal study record.

docs.title: Children and audience
docs.text: Stutastic Planner is intended for students generally and is not specifically directed to children under 13. The app does not ask you to enter your age or date of birth. If you have a question about a child's use of the app or their information, submit a Private report at support.danplace.tech/p/stu/report.

docs.title: Changes to this policy
docs.text: If this policy changes, the updated version and its date will be published on this page.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
Everything in Stutastic Planner hangs off your semester: its dates and periods, the subjects you take in it, and their classes. Tasks, tests, study topics, attendance and focus time all belong to a subject, so the app can show them together and work out your grades.

Feature What it does Page Dashboard Today's classes, what's due, attendance warnings, GPA, focus time and trends Dashboard Planner Your timetable and calendar by day, week or month; add, cancel or move classes Planner Agenda, events and holidays Everything due in one list; one-off events; days with no classes Agenda, events and holidays University import Bring subjects, classes and results in from your student portal Import from your university Tasks Assignments with a due date and progress Tasks Study topics Revision progress per topic, linked to the tests they're for Study topics Quizzes and exams Test dates, seats, scores and the topics they cover Quizzes and exams Subjects and academics Programmes, semesters, periods, marks, grades, GPA and CGPA Subjects and academics Attendance The classes you miss, and how close you are to being barred Attendance Focus sessions A Pomodoro timer that logs time against your work Focus sessions Reminders Notifications before class and about what's due Reminders Settings Appearance, Google Calendar, account, backups and more Settings

docs.title: What differs by platform
docs.text:
iPhone and iPad Android Mac Windows and Linux Web Works offline Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes, once loaded Reminders Yes Yes Yes Yes (Linux: while Planner is running) No Focus timer outside the app Lock Screen and Dynamic Island Notification — — — Keep a university login for timetable refresh Yes Yes Yes Yes No IIUM timetable import Yes Yes Yes Yes No Menu bar and keyboard shortcuts Shortcuts with a keyboard Shortcuts with a keyboard Menu bar and shortcuts Shortcuts Shortcuts Sign in with Apple Yes — Yes — —

Everything else, including Google Calendar, backups and sync, works the same on every platform.

docs.title: Subjects and academics
docs.text: Your programme holds years, the years hold semesters, and each semester holds the subjects you take in it. Everything else in the app belongs to a subject, and your grades roll up into a semester GPA and a CGPA.

docs.title: Subjects
docs.text:
Open Subjects to see this semester's subjects with their codes and credits. Tap one to open it.

A subject has six tabs:

Tab Shows Details Code, section, teacher, credits and how it's graded Schedule Its weekly classes Attendance How much you've missed, and every class so far with its mark. See Attendance Tasks Its tasks, with the number still open on the tab Tests Its quizzes, tests and exams Grades Your marks so far, your standing and the grade you're heading for

On a tablet in landscape or a large window, the subject opens beside the list.

docs.title: Add or edit a subject
docs.text:
Tap + on Subjects, or open a subject and choose Edit. Enter:

  • Subject name and Code, such as "Data Structures and Algorithms" and "CSC 2103";
  • Credits, which weight the subject in your GPA;
  • Grading: Graded for a letter grade that counts toward your GPA, or Pass / Fail, Audit or Exempted for one that doesn't;
  • Final grade, once you have it;
  • optionally the Teacher and Section, and your own Warn at % and Barred at % lines for attendance.

Turn on Archived to hide a subject from the list while keeping its grade.

docs.title: Marks and grades
docs.text:
The Grades tab works out where you stand before the final grade is in. Set it up once per subject, from Edit → Grades:

  1. Add category for each part of the assessment, such as Assignments, Quizzes and Final Exam, with its Weight (%), its share of the final grade. The weights should add up to 100.
  2. In each category, Add mark for each piece of work. Link a Quiz or Task to read its score from there, or choose Custom and type the Score and what it's Out of.

The tab then shows your Current standing, a percentage of the marks given so far, and the Est. grade it would earn on your grading scale. Categories with nothing in them yet, such as a final exam still to come, show no marks yet and don't count against you.

When the subject's final grade is set, its final exam's score is worked out from it.

docs.title: Academics
docs.text: Academics has four tabs: Semesters, Years, Programmes and Grading. The top shows your Cumulative GPA and the credits you've Fulfilled.

docs.title: Semesters and periods
docs.text:
Open a semester for two tabs:

  • Overview: its GPA, its credits and grading scale, Right now (which period you're in), the Cumulative up to here CGPA, and every period in the term.
  • Classes: each subject in it with its credits and grade.

Choose Edit to change it, in two parts: Details (name, dates and grading) and Periods.

A semester's periods divide it up: lectures, break, revision, exam, holiday, or a custom period with your own name, such as an orientation week, and its own "classes run" and "counts as a teaching week" switches. Periods:

  • number the teaching weeks in the Planner;
  • stop classes on days in a break, exam or holiday period, and tint those days in the month view;
  • set the Week A anchor date for alternating classes.

A new period starts where the last one ended, so you mostly adjust end dates and choose types.

The app opens on the semester that covers today, not the newest one you created, and tells you when you're looking at one that hasn't started yet or has already ended.

docs.title: From your university's calendar
docs.text:
If your programme is at a university that publishes its academic calendar (IIUM does), the app can fill semesters in from it:

  • A new semester: Fill from IIUM's calendar lists the calendar's semesters you don't have yet. Pick one and its name, dates and periods are filled in, and it's placed in your programme's year for that session.
  • A semester you already have: its page shows Use IIUM's calendar dates with the calendar's dates. Tap it to see a summary of the dates and periods, then Use these dates. Close it if you'd rather keep your own; it won't ask again for that semester.
  • When the university changes its calendar: a semester filled from it shows IIUM updated Sem 1, 2026/2027, on the dashboard and on the semester's page. Tap it to see what changed and Update, or close it to keep your dates.

Nothing changes until you accept. Your own edits to dates and periods stay yours.

docs.title: Programmes
docs.text:
Most students have one programme. Add another for a second course of study, such as a minor or a programme change part-way through. Switching the active programme switches everything else in the app to that programme's semesters and subjects. A programme can set default grading for its new semesters.

Studying abroad? A programme can have its own time zone

If your programme is based somewhere other than where you are (an exchange semester, or a remote degree in another country), open the programme and set its time zone. Classes, tests and due times under it are entered in that time zone, shown in the time zone you're in, and reminded at the right moment. Leave it unset to use your device's time zone. See Time zones.

If you're exempted from a subject under another programme, such as a transfer credit, mark it from the subject's details with Exempt to another programme. Exemptions can be edited or removed later from that programme's own page.

docs.title: Grading scales and GPA
docs.text:
Grading lists your grading scales: each grade, its points and its minimum percentage. A semester uses one scale, and your GPA and the Est. grade on each subject come from it.

As you enter grades, the app works out each semester's GPA and your CGPA.

\"~\" means an estimate

A GPA shown with a leading ~, such as ~3.81, still includes subjects without a final grade, using their estimated grades. Once every subject in the semester has a final grade, the ~ goes.

If your university publishes its grading scale (IIUM does), Settings → Your university shows Use IIUM's grading scale when yours differs, for example a D worth 1.00 instead of 1.67. Tap it to see which grades change and use the university's points. Your semesters keep the scale they use, now with the right points.

docs.title: Attendance
docs.text: Many universities stop students from sitting a course's final exam when they miss too much of it. Attendance keeps a record of each class you miss and shows, for every subject, how close you are to a warning or to being barred.

docs.title: How it counts
docs.text:
Only classes you mark Absent count as missed.

Mark Counts as Present Attended Late Attended, shown as late Absent Missed Excused Not held against you, for example with a medical certificate

Any mark can carry a short note, such as "MC".

Missed time is measured against the whole term: every class of the subject from the first day of the semester to the last, including the ones still to come. Excused classes stay in that total. Cancelled classes and holidays are not part of it. A class moved to another day counts on its new times.

By default it counts hours, so a 1.5-hour class is 1.5 hours of the term. You can count classes instead, so that every class counts the same.

docs.title: The warning and barring lines
docs.text:
Two lines are set as a percentage of the term:

  • Warn at: 10% by default;
  • Barred at: 20% by default.

A line is reached the moment you get to it, not only after you pass it. Numbers are rounded toward the stricter side, so the app never shows you safer than you are.

A subject can set its own lines. Open the subject, choose Edit, and fill in Warn at % or Barred at % under Attendance. Leave a field empty to use your setting.

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text:
• The Dashboard shows an Attendance warnings card when a subject you have missed classes in is close to a line or past it, worst first: "Can miss 1 more before barring", "Next missed class bars you", "Barred". Tap a subject to open its Attendance tab. With nothing close, there is no card. You can move or hide it with Customize dashboard, like the other cards.
  • A subject's Attendance tab shows a bar, the hours missed ("3 h of 42 h missed (7.2%)"), both lines, and how many more classes you can miss before each. Below it, Recent classes lists every class held so far, newest first, each with its mark.
  • A class's details show one line, such as "3 h of 42 h missed". Tap it to open the subject's Attendance tab.

docs.title: Alerts
docs.text:
Choose how the app warns you in Settings → Attendance → Alerts:

  • Quiet: colours only, no messages.
  • Nudge (the default): when marking a class takes a subject past a line, a message says so straight away, for example "Data Structures (CS201) reached the warning: 10% missed · can miss 3 more classes before barring". You also get one when the next missed class would bar you.
  • Before class: the same, plus a line on the class reminder when missing that class would take you past a line, such as "Missing it would reach the warning line (10%)". This needs class reminders turned on in Settings → Reminders; the Attendance settings say so if they are off.

Nothing appears until you have missed at least one class.

docs.title: Marking a class
docs.text:
Each class carries a small icon for its mark: on the Planner beside its time, and on the subject's Attendance tab.

Icon Mark Green tick Present Clock Late Red cross Absent Badge Excused Grey tick Not marked, counted as present Question mark Not marked, under Ask or Only what I mark Empty circle Still to come

Tap the icon to choose a mark, add a note, or clear it. You can mark a future class Absent or Excused ahead of time, for a trip you already know about.

docs.title: Marking
docs.text:
Choose how unmarked classes are treated in Settings → Attendance → Marking. The numbers are the same in every mode, because only Absent counts as missed.

  • Assume present (the default): a class you never mark counts as present, and nothing asks you.
  • Ask: after each class a notification asks how it went, with Present, Absent and Excused buttons. A button opens the app and records the mark, with an Undo. Classes you have not answered show as Not marked, and the Dashboard lists the last week's in a Not marked yet card, where you can mark each one from its icon. These notifications do not need class reminders turned on. The web app has no notifications, so there you mark from the card.
  • Only what I mark: unmarked classes stay Not marked, with no prompts. Each subject's Attendance tab shows how much you have marked, such as "Marked 18 of 24 past hours".

A class counts as past once it has ended.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Go to Settings → Attendance to:

  • turn Track attendance off, which hides everything above;
  • choose whether to count by hours or classes;
  • set the Warn at and Barred at lines;
  • choose the Alerts: Quiet, Nudge or Before class;
  • choose how you mark: Assume present, Ask or Only what I mark.

Your marks sync to your other devices and are included in backups.

docs.title: Agenda
docs.text:
The Agenda lists everything that's due, across all your subjects, in three groups: Overdue, Due soon and Later. It's the quickest way to answer "what do I still have to do?". Find it under Planner on a phone, or in the sidebar on wider screens.

  • The Tasks, Tests and Study buttons at the top show or hide each kind.
  • Each row shows its subject and how long is left, such as Tomorrow or In 3 days; overdue work shows how late it is in red.
  • Tap a row to open it. Finished work drops off the list.
  • With nothing left, the Agenda says Nothing outstanding.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
An event is anything with a date that isn't a class or coursework: a careers fair, a club meeting, a hackathon weekend.

  1. Tap + on the Planner, Dashboard or Agenda and choose Add event.
  2. Enter a Title and the Starts and Ends dates. An event can span several days.
  3. Add Notes if you like. Notes support Markdown, so you can use lists, bold text and links.
  4. Choose Save.

Events show in the Planner on their days and along the top of the week view.

docs.title: Holidays
docs.text:
A holiday is a day, or several, when classes will not meet, such as a public holiday.

  1. Tap + and choose Add holiday, or choose Holiday at the top of a new entry.
  2. Enter a title and its dates, then Save.

Classes on those days disappear from the Planner, the Dashboard and your reminders, and don't count toward attendance.

Holiday or period?

For a single day off, add a holiday. For a stretch of the semester, such as a mid-semester break, revision week or the exam weeks, add a period to the semester in Academics instead. Periods also renumber the teaching weeks and tint those days in the month view.

If you study in one time zone and your university is in another, holidays follow the university's calendar. See Time zones.

docs.title: Google Calendar
docs.text: To see your classes, tasks and tests in Google Calendar, connect it in Settings → Google Calendar. Stutastic Planner keeps a calendar of its own there and updates it as your planner changes. For a one-off file instead, use Export to a calendar.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text: The Dashboard is the first screen you see. It answers "what's on today, and what's coming?" for your current semester, and gathers the numbers you'd otherwise look up across several screens.

docs.title: The cards
docs.text:
From the top, in their usual order:

Card Shows Stats row Semester GPA (a ~ in front means some grades are still estimates), your focus Streak in days, and how many things are Due soon in the next 7 days Attendance warnings Subjects close to the warning or barring line, worst first. Only appears when one is. See Attendance Not marked yet The last week's classes waiting for a mark, when you mark attendance with Ask Today's classes Today's classes with their times and rooms. Cancelled and moved classes are already accounted for Due soon Tasks and tests coming up, with how long you have left Focus time by subject Where your focus time went, this Week or this Semester Test score trend Your quiz and test scores over time Focus suggestions Study topics to revise next: those linked to the nearest tests and furthest from done come first Quote of the day Something to read before you start

Tap any row to open it. Your streak counts days with at least one finished focus block; today not having one yet doesn't break it.

Nothing on the Dashboard?

The Dashboard needs a semester. With none, it shows No semester yet and an Add a semester button. Cards fill in as you use the app: the test trend, for example, says No graded tests yet. until a test has a score.

docs.title: Add from the Dashboard
docs.text: Tap + at the top to add a class, task, test, topic, event or holiday without leaving the screen.

docs.title: Customise it
docs.text:
Tap the sliders button at the top right to open Customize dashboard. Switch off any card you don't use, move cards with the up and down arrows, then choose Save. Reset puts everything back.

The layout is kept per device, so your phone can show a short list while your computer shows everything.

docs.title: On wider screens
docs.text: On a tablet in landscape or a large window, the Dashboard uses two columns: your day on the left and Due soon and Focus suggestions on the right.

docs.title: Dark mode
docs.text: The Dashboard, like the rest of the app, follows your device's light or dark appearance unless you choose one in Settings → Appearance.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text: Tasks are your assignments, reports, problem sets and anything else you have to hand in. Each one belongs to a subject, can have a due date, and has a progress bar you move as you work on it.

docs.title: Add a task
docs.text:
1. Open Tasks (under Coursework on a phone) and tap +. You can also add one from the + on the Planner or Dashboard, or press ⌘N (Ctrl+N).
  2. Enter a Title and choose the Subject.
  3. Set Due if it has a deadline. Leave it at No due date for work without one.
  4. Time is End of the day unless you pick a time, for a submission that closes at 5 PM, for example.
  5. Choose Save.

docs.title: The list
docs.text:
Tasks are listed with the soonest due first. Each row shows its subject and how long you have left, such as Today, Tomorrow, In 3 days or 1 day overdue. Finished tasks are struck through with a green tick at the bottom.

On a tablet in landscape or a large window, the selected task opens beside the list.

docs.title: Track progress
docs.text:
Open a task and drag its Progress slider as you go, in steps of 5%. At 100% the task is Completed. Mark done jumps straight there.

Until a task is done, it stays in Due soon on the Dashboard and in the Agenda.

docs.title: Work on it
docs.text: Start Pomodoro on a task starts a focus session on it, and the time you spend is logged against its subject. The timer button at the top of the Tasks list starts a session where you can pick several tasks at once.

docs.title: Edit or delete
docs.text:
Open the task and choose Edit to change it, or Delete to remove it. Focus time already logged against a deleted task is kept in your totals.

On a Mac, right-click a task in the list for Mark done and its other actions.

docs.title: Reminders
docs.text: With reminders on, the app tells you what's due today before your first class, and what's due tomorrow after your last one.

docs.title: Reminders
docs.text: Stutastic Planner can remind you before each class and about what's due. Reminders are scheduled on your device, so they arrive even when you're offline, and they don't need an account. They're off until you turn them on.

docs.title: Turn reminders on
docs.text:
1. Open Settings → Reminders and turn on Remind me. You can also turn them on during setup, at Never miss a class.
  2. Allow notifications when your device asks.

If you said no to notifications earlier, turn them on for Stutastic Planner in your device's settings, then come back.

docs.title: What you're reminded about
docs.text:
Reminder When Before a class starts 5, 10, 15, 30 or 60 minutes before each class (10 by default) What is due today An hour before your first class of the day What is due tomorrow After your last class of the day

Cancelled classes, moved classes and holidays are taken into account. With attendance alerts set to Before class, a class reminder also tells you when missing that class would take you past a line.

Open the app every two weeks

Reminders are scheduled two weeks ahead. Open the app at least that often so it can schedule the next two weeks.

Turning Remind me off cancels every reminder already scheduled on the device.

docs.title: By platform
docs.text:
• iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac and Windows: reminders arrive whether or not the app is open.
  • Linux: reminders arrive only while Planner is running. Start at login and Keep running in the tray, on this page, keep it running in the background; closing the window then leaves it in the tray.
  • Web: reminders aren't available. Use one of the apps, or connect Google Calendar and let it remind you.

Reminders are set per device: turn them on on each device you want them on.

docs.title: Focus sessions
docs.text: A focus session is a Pomodoro timer: blocks of focused work with short breaks between them and a longer break every few blocks. You choose what you're working on first, so the time is logged against the right subject and you can tick things off as you finish them.

docs.title: Start a session
docs.text:
On one thing: open a task, topic or test and choose Start Pomodoro (Focus with Pomodoro on a test). The timer starts straight away on it.

On a list of things: tap the timer button at the top of Tasks, Study or Quizzes, or press ⇧⌘F (Ctrl+Shift+F). Then three short steps:

  1. What are you working on? Tick one or more tasks, tests and study topics, in the order you'll do them, then Next.
  2. Session settings. The Number of sessions, the Session length, the Short break and Long break in minutes, and how often the long break comes (Long break every). The defaults are 4 × 25 minutes with 5-minute breaks and a 15-minute long break. Then Next.
  3. Ready to start. The whole session as a bar of focus and break blocks, with the total time. Choose Start.

docs.title: While it runs
docs.text:
The timer shows as a bar above the tabs, so you can keep using the app. Tap it to open the full timer.

The full timer has three buttons:

Button Does Skip phase Ends this focus block or break now and moves to the next Pause / resume Stops the clock until you resume. Space does the same with a keyboard Finished this one Marks what you're on as done, and moves to the next thing in your list

Finished this one completes a task and takes a study topic to 100%. A test isn't changed: you've finished studying for it, not sitting it.

The arrow at the top shrinks the full timer back to the bar.

Outside the app:

  • iPhone: the timer stays on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island. The Lock Screen shows the phase, what you're working on and the time left, with the whole session as a bar underneath: blocks you've finished are solid, the one you're in fills up as you go, and breaks are green. It also says when this block and the whole session end. The card turns green on a break and grey while paused.
  • Android: an ongoing notification shows the phase, the time left and a bar for the whole session. On Android 16 and later the bar is split into your focus blocks and breaks.

The timer keeps time even if the app is closed: come back and it's where it should be.

docs.title: When your list is done
docs.text:
When you've finished everything you ticked, the app asks Nothing left in your list. What next?

  • Keep focusing carries on without an item.
  • Add more items goes back to the list.
  • End session stops and saves the session.

docs.title: Where the time goes
docs.text:
Every focus block you finish is logged against the subject of what you were working on. It shows on the Dashboard in Focus time by subject, for this week or this semester, and keeps your Streak going.

Focus sessions work offline. Signed in, they sync to your other devices; deleting a task later keeps the time already logged against it.

docs.title: Quizzes and exams
docs.text: Keep every quiz, test and final exam in one list, with its date, its seat, the topics it covers and, afterwards, your score.

docs.title: Add a quiz or test
docs.text:
1. Open Quizzes (under Coursework on a phone) and tap +, or press ⌥⌘Q (Ctrl+Alt+Q).
  2. Leave Quiz or test selected. Enter a Title, such as "Quiz 3: Trees", and choose the Subject.
  3. Set the Date, and a start and end time if you know them. Pick a start time and the end is filled in from your default class length.
  4. Under Topics covered, tick the study topics it tests. Only the subject's own topics are listed.
  5. Choose Save.

Once it's graded, open it, choose Edit, and enter the Score and what it's Out of. Scores feed the Dashboard's Test score trend and, if you give the subject marks categories, its grade.

No need to close it yourself

Once a quiz's date has passed, it shows as completed, with or without a score. Add the score whenever it comes back.

docs.title: Add a final exam
docs.text:
Choose Final Exam at the top of the form. It adds:

  • Seat or table number, shown in the list and the details, so you know where to go on the day;
  • a default end time from your default exam length, which you set in Settings → Class and exam lengths.

A final exam's score isn't typed in. It's worked back from the subject's final grade once you set it under Subjects.

Add a Notes line for anything you'll need on the day, such as "Bring your student card".

docs.title: Before the test
docs.text:
Open a test to see its Related topics, each with its progress, and an Overall figure for how ready you are. Focus with Pomodoro starts a focus session on it.

The nearest tests also drive the Dashboard's Focus suggestions, which list the linked topics you're least ready for first.

docs.title: Time zones
docs.text: If your programme has its own time zone (see Programmes), a test's date and time are entered in that time zone and shown in the time zone you're in. Most people never need this.

docs.title: Planner
docs.text: The Planner is your timetable and calendar in one. It shows your classes for the semester, together with tasks, tests, events and holidays, by Day, Week or Month.

docs.title: Move around
docs.text:
• Switch between Day, Week and Month at the top.
  • Use the arrows to go back or forward, and Today to come back.
  • Month numbers each teaching week (W1, W2 …) and tints days that fall in a break, revision or exam period. Tap a day to list its items underneath, with the period and week, such as "Lectures · Week 8".
  • Week puts deadlines along the top and classes in the grid. A red line marks the time now. The magnifier buttons zoom the hours in and out.
  • Tap any class or item to open it.

On a tablet in landscape or a large window, the week view shows all seven days at once.

docs.title: Add a class
docs.text:
Tap + and choose Add class. The same menu adds a task, test, study topic, event or holiday.

  1. Choose the Subject. Add the subject first in Subjects if it isn't there.
  2. Tick one or more Days. A class on Monday and Wednesday at the same time is one class.
  3. Set Starts and Ends, and an optional Location.
  4. Under Repeats, choose Weekly, or Every 2 weeks for a class that alternates. See Alternating weeks.
  5. Starts in week and Ends after week limit a class to part of the term, such as a lab that begins in Week 3. Leave Ends after week at Semester end to run to the end of term.
  6. Choose Save.

When you pick a start time first, the end time is filled in from your default class length in Settings → Class and exam lengths. Change it if this class runs longer.

docs.title: Class details
docs.text: Tap a class to see its day, times, location, how it repeats and which weeks it runs. If you track attendance, a line such as "0 h of 42 h missed (0%)" shows how much of the subject you've missed; tap it to open the subject's Attendance tab.

docs.title: Cancel or move one date
docs.text:
Classes get cancelled and moved. Change one date without touching the rest of the term:

  • Cancel a date removes the class on one date. The date you opened the class from is filled in; choose another if you need to.
  • Reschedule a date moves one date to another day and time: pick the date, then where it's Moved to, with its Start and End.

The change shows everywhere: the Planner, the Dashboard, reminders, attendance and Google Calendar. To cancel classes for a public holiday across all your subjects, add a holiday instead.

Edit changes the class for the whole term. Delete removes the class after asking.

docs.title: Alternating weeks
docs.text:
For a class that meets every other week:

  1. Open the semester in Academics, choose Edit, and on Periods set the Week A anchor date: the first day of a Week A.
  2. Add or edit the class, set Repeats to Every 2 weeks, and choose Which week: Week A or Week B.

Weeks A and B then alternate from that date.

docs.title: Bring in a timetable
docs.text: The ⋯ menu at the top of the Planner has three ways to add classes in bulk, and one way out:

docs.title: Import from your university
docs.text: Signs in to your student portal and brings in your subjects and classes. See Import from your university.

docs.title: Paste a timetable
docs.text:
Type or paste one class per line: the subject code, the day, the start and end times, and optionally the location, the week (all, a or b) and how it repeats (weekly or biweekly). For example:

CSC 2103,mon,09:00,11:00,Lecture Hall 2
CSC 2103,wed,14:00,16:00,Computer Lab 3
CSC 2301,fri,09:00,10:00,Room B210,a,biweekly

Choose Preview to check the rows, match each code to a subject, then Import.

docs.title: Export to a calendar
docs.text: Saves an .ics file of the semester's classes. Open it in Apple Calendar, Google Calendar, Outlook or any calendar app that reads iCalendar files. It's a one-off copy; for a calendar that stays up to date, connect Google Calendar.

docs.title: Time zones
docs.text:
Classes use the time zone set for their programme. If the programme has no time zone set, your device's time zone is used. When you travel, times are shown in the time zone you're in.

A class from another time zone can land on a different day for you. A Monday morning class in Kuala Lumpur, for example, happens on Sunday evening in New York. Holidays, term dates and teaching weeks still follow the university's own calendar, so that class is off when the university's Monday is a holiday, whatever the date where you are. Cancelling or moving one class uses the day it shows on in your Planner.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Settings is a list of pages. On a phone, tap a row to open it. On a tablet in landscape or a large window, the page opens beside the list.

Page What it's for Appearance Light or dark, the clock, and subject codes Reminders Class and deadline reminders on this device Google Calendar A calendar in your Google account that follows your planner Your university Where you study, timetable import, and kept logins Class and exam lengths Default lengths and named exam start times Attendance Tracking, the warning and barring lines, alerts and marking Password & email Your sign-in details Account Sync status, sign out, or delete your account Your data Export a backup or restore one Privacy Usage analytics About Version, this site, support and updates

docs.title: Appearance
docs.text:
• System, Light or Dark. System follows your device, so the app changes with it.
  • Time: System, 12-hour or 24-hour. The line underneath shows how times will look, such as "2:30 – 3:50 PM".
  • Show subject codes: show each subject as "Name (CODE)" in lists, pickers and the Planner. Turn it off for names only.

These are kept on this device, so your phone and computer can differ.

docs.title: Reminders
docs.text: Turn on Remind me, then choose what you're reminded about. See Reminders.

docs.title: Google Calendar
docs.text:
Google Calendar is optional and needs a Stutastic Planner account. A guest sees Sign in here first.

  1. Open Settings → Google Calendar and choose Connect Google Calendar.
  2. Sign in to Google and allow access.

Planner then creates a calendar of its own in your Google account and keeps your classes, tasks and tests in it as your planner changes. It never touches your other calendars. Let Google Calendar remind me too adds Google's own reminders to those events. It's off by default; turn it on if you'd like Google to remind you as well as the app.

Disconnect stops the connection and asks Google to remove the Planner calendar. Deleting your account disconnects it too. If the app can't confirm the calendar was removed, account deletion stops so you can try again. Google may sometimes leave the calendar behind; you can then delete it in Google Calendar yourself.

On Apple devices: \"no authorisation code\"

If connecting fails with this message, Google already has Stutastic Planner listed from an earlier connection. Remove Stutastic Planner from your Google account's third-party access, then connect again.

docs.title: Your university
docs.text: Where you study and what the app does for it: Import timetable, changing university, and the semesters kept up to date with your portal, with Refresh now and Forget my login. Keeping a login isn't available on the web. See Import from your university.

docs.title: Class and exam lengths
docs.text:
• Default class length (minutes) fills in a class's or a quiz's end time when you pick its start.
  • Default exam length (minutes) does the same for a final exam.
  • Exam sessions are named start times, such as "Morning, 9:00 AM", to pick from when you schedule an exam. Choose Add to add one.

docs.title: Password & email
docs.text: Change the password or email address you sign in with.

docs.title: Account
docs.text:
• As a guest: Create an account to sync keeps everything you have and starts syncing it. Leave without saving deletes the guest data on this device, after asking.
  • Signed in: shows whether your changes have synced. Sign out keeps your account and clears this device. Delete my account removes the account and its synced data.

If the server ever refuses a change, Changes that couldn't be saved appears here with a Review button. Each change can be tried again or discarded; nothing is lost until you discard it.

Leaving, signing out and deleting all leave the device as if the app had just been installed. See Guest mode vs. an account.

docs.title: Your data
docs.text: Export everything saves a backup file. Restore from a backup loads one, merged with what you have or replacing it. See Export and import.

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text: Usage analytics turns anonymous usage statistics on or off for this device. See the Privacy Policy.

docs.title: About
docs.text: The installed Version, a link to this Documentation, and Support for searching issues or reporting a bug. On Windows and Linux, Check for updates looks for a newer version; other platforms update from their app store. The app also tells you when a new version is ready.

docs.title: Study topics
docs.text: Study topics break a subject into the chapters or topics you need to revise, so you can see how ready you are for each test. Tasks are for work you hand in; topics are for what you need to know.

docs.title: Add a topic
docs.text:
1. Open Study (under Coursework on a phone) and tap +, or press ⌥⌘S (Ctrl+Alt+S).
  2. Enter the Topic and choose the Subject.
  3. Topic number keeps topics in the order you'll study them, such as the lecture or chapter number.
  4. Revise by is an optional date of your own, such as the night before the test.
  5. Set Progress if you've already started, then Save.

docs.title: The list
docs.text:
Topics are grouped by subject. Each row shows its topic number, a progress bar, and a chip for every test it's linked to, such as Midterm test or Final Exam. Finished topics are struck through with a green tick.

Open a topic and drag its progress as you revise. At 100% it's done.

docs.title: Link topics to tests
docs.text:
When you add or edit a quiz, test or final exam, tick the subject's topics under Topics covered. Then:

  • the topic shows that test's chip in the Study list;
  • the test shows its topics and an overall progress, so you can see how ready you are;
  • the Dashboard's Focus suggestions puts the topics for your nearest tests that are furthest from done at the top.

docs.title: Revise with focus sessions
docs.text: Start a focus session on a topic, from the timer button at the top of Study or the topic's own details. The time counts toward the subject in your focus summaries.

docs.title: Import from your university
docs.text: If your university is supported, Stutastic Planner can sign in to your student portal and bring in a semester's subjects and weekly classes, so you don't have to type them in.

docs.title: Supported universities
docs.text:
The app lists the universities it can import from, with the name of each one's portal. The list currently includes IIUM (i-Ma'luum), UiTM, IIC, APU, UniKL, UTM and UPSI. Universities are added as the import service gains support for them.

IIUM's import is available in the app on your phone, tablet or computer, but not on the web.

docs.title: Import a semester
docs.text:
You can start an import from four places:

  • the Bring in your timetable step of first-run setup;
  • Settings → Your university → Import timetable;
  • Planner menu → Import from your university;
  • a semester's details → Import timetable.

When the app knows your university (you chose it in setup or in Settings → Your university), the import starts at signing in. Otherwise it asks which university first, and remembers it.

Then:

  1. Choose your university. The app remembers your choice on this device.
  2. Sign in with your student ID and portal password. Your student ID is remembered on this device; your password is not, unless you choose to stay signed in (see below). The app shows each step as it signs in and loads your timetable. If you signed in recently, or chose to stay signed in, choose Continue as your student ID instead, with no typing; Use a different account shows the fields.
  3. Choose the semesters to import: tick one or more. The current semester is ticked for you, and older semesters load when you tick them.
  4. Choose where each goes.
    • A new semester: named from your portal, for example "Sem 1, 2026/2027". Enter its start and end dates. It goes into the year named for its session, for example "2025/2026", if you have one, or else into a new year with that name; you can choose another. If your university publishes its academic calendar, the dates are filled in for you, marked From IIUM's calendar, and the semester gets the calendar's periods. Change the dates and it's saved as you typed it instead. You'll see a warning if a new semester's dates overlap another semester's.
    • A semester you already have: one with the same name is chosen for you. If you started from a semester's details, the newest import goes there.
    • No programme yet: if you haven't set one up, one is created for your university, with its grading scale when the university publishes one.
  5. Review. Each semester has its own section. Each subject shows its code, name, credit hours, section, lecturer and weekly classes, marked New or Already here. Untick anything you don't want.
  6. Import. The app adds what you ticked, oldest semester first, and the newest becomes the semester you're looking at. If something stops part-way, what was already imported stays, and trying again won't duplicate it.

docs.title: What an import changes
docs.text:
• New subjects are added with their code, name, credit hours, section, lecturer and a colour.
  • Subjects you already have are matched by their code. Only their empty details are filled in; names and anything you typed are kept.
  • Classes are matched by day and start time. A matching class gets the portal's end time and room and keeps its own colour, week pattern and exceptions; anything else is added.
  • Nothing is removed. Classes in the app that aren't in the import stay as they are.

Importing the same semester again changes nothing.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
For IIUM, each semester's results come with it, so your GPA and CGPA are right without typing your grades.

  • Grades: each subject's grade comes in with its credit hours. A pass (PA) becomes a Pass / Fail subject. So does a grade your portal gives no grade point, such as IIUM's co-curricular courses: it doesn't count in your CGPA.
  • Pass / Fail subjects saved as graded are offered the change, for example "A here, pass/fail at i-Ma'luum, so not in your CGPA".
  • Grades you typed: a grade you've already entered that differs from your portal's is shown as, for example, "B+ here, A at i-Ma'luum". Yours is kept unless you tick it.
  • Subjects with results but no classes, such as a final-year project, are still added.
  • The grading scale: if your programme's scale gives a grade different points from your portal's, for example "D: 1.00 here, 1.67 at i-Ma'luum", the review offers to fix it. That's ticked for you.
  • The CGPA check: after importing, the app shows its CGPA next to your portal's. If they differ, check repeated or exempted subjects.

Semesters without results yet, such as the current one, import their timetable only. Results aren't refreshed automatically; import the semester again when new results are released.

docs.title: Keep your timetable up to date
docs.text:
On the sign-in step, tick Keep me signed in to refresh my timetable if you'd like the app to notice changes at your university, such as a class moved to another room or time, or a subject added or dropped. This option isn't available on the web.

  • Only your portal's current semester is kept up to date. If you import only past semesters, your password is still kept, so next time Continue as can link the current one.

  • Continuing while still signed in from earlier? Tick Keep me signed in there and enter your password once.

  • The app checks at most once a day, when you open it or come back to it, and only when you're online.

  • If something changed, the Dashboard and Planner show Your timetable changed. Choose Review to see each change.
    • Changes are ticked to apply, except for classes you changed yourself, which are kept unless you tick them.
    • A subject dropped at your university can have its classes removed; the subject itself stays.
    • Choose Apply to make the ticked changes, or Ignore to leave your timetable as it is.
  • If your portal stops accepting the kept password (for example after you change it), the app deletes it and asks you to Sign in again.

To see which semesters are kept up to date, check now, or stop, go to Settings → Your university and choose Refresh now or Forget my login. Signing out or deleting your account also deletes every kept login.

docs.title: Your password
docs.text:
• IIUM: the app signs in to i-Ma'luum directly from your device. Your password goes only to IIUM's sign-in page, over an encrypted connection, and never to us.
  • Other universities: your password is sent over an encrypted connection to the Stutastic Planner import service, only so it can sign in to your university's portal for you. The service doesn't store or log it.
  • If you choose to stay signed in, the password is kept only on your device, in its secure storage (the Keychain on Apple devices, Keystore-protected storage on Android). It's never synced to your account or included in exports.

See the privacy policy for details.

docs.title: Guest mode vs. an account
docs.text: You can use Stutastic Planner without creating an account.

docs.title: Guest mode
docs.text: At the end of setup, choose Not now, keep it on this device. Your planner records are stored on that device and are not synced to an account. Guest mode works offline, but uninstalling the app, clearing its local data, or losing the device can remove the only copy of those records. Use Export everything to keep a backup.

docs.title: Using an account
docs.text:
Sign in with Google or email; Apple sign-in is available on Apple platforms. An account lets the app sync planner records across devices when they are online. A network connection is needed to sign in and sync.

If you start as a guest, you can create an account later from Settings → Account using Create an account to sync. Your existing planner data comes with you. You can also export a backup and restore it on another device; see Export and Import.

docs.title: Signing out or deleting data
docs.text:
Leave without saving ends a guest session. It asks first, then deletes everything the guest stored on the device. Create an account first if you want to keep it.

For a signed-in account, Sign out keeps the cloud account, while Delete my account removes the account and its synced planner records.

Leaving guest mode, signing out and deleting an account all leave the device as if the app had just been installed: - planner data is removed from the device; - university logins kept for refreshing your timetable are deleted; - scheduled reminders are cancelled; - your settings on that device go back to their defaults: theme, clock, reminders and layout.

Only your choice about usage analytics is kept. Export a backup first if you want to keep a copy. Account deletion also attempts to disconnect Google Calendar. If the app cannot confirm cleanup, deletion stops so you can retry or disconnect from Settings → Google Calendar.

docs.title: Getting around
docs.text:
Stutastic Planner has nine screens. The layout changes with the width of the screen or window, but the screens are the same everywhere:

Screen What it's for Dashboard Today's classes, what's due, attendance warnings and your study summaries Planner Your timetable and calendar by day, week or month Agenda Everything due, overdue first, in one list Tasks Assignments and other work with a due date Study Revision topics, grouped by subject Quizzes Quizzes, tests and final exams Subjects Each subject's details, schedule, attendance, work and grades Academics Programmes, years, semesters, GPA and CGPA Settings Preferences, reminders, account and backups

docs.title: On a phone
docs.text:
The bar at the bottom has four buttons: Dashboard, Planner, Coursework and Settings. Planner and Coursework hold more than one screen. Tap one to choose:

  • Planner → Planner or Agenda;
  • Coursework → Tasks, Study, Quizzes, Subjects or Academics.

Tap + at the top of a screen to add something, and tap a row to open its details.

docs.title: On a tablet or a wider window
docs.text:
On an iPad, an Android tablet, or a desktop window of medium width, every screen has its own button in a rail down the left side.

On wider screens, such as an iPad in landscape or a large desktop window, the rail opens out into a labelled sidebar in three groups: Today (Dashboard, Planner, Agenda), Coursework (Tasks, Study, Quizzes) and School (Subjects, Academics).

Lists also show the selected item beside them, so you can go down a list without opening and closing each one. Nothing selected shows until you pick a row.

docs.title: Keyboard shortcuts
docs.text:
With a keyboard attached (a Mac, Windows or Linux computer, an iPad or Android tablet with a keyboard, or the web app), these shortcuts work anywhere in the app. On a Mac, an iPad, or the web app on a Mac, use the first column; on Windows, Linux and Android, use the second.

Action Mac and iPad Windows, Linux and Android New task ⌘N Ctrl+N New event ⇧⌘N Ctrl+Shift+N New class ⌥⌘C Ctrl+Alt+C New quiz ⌥⌘Q Ctrl+Alt+Q New study topic ⌥⌘S Ctrl+Alt+S Go to a screen, in the order of the table above ⌘1 to ⌘9 Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+9 Planner: day, week or month view ⌃⌘1, ⌃⌘2, ⌃⌘3 Alt+1, Alt+2, Alt+3 Planner: today ⌘T Ctrl+T Planner: previous or next ⌘[ and ⌘] Ctrl+[ and Ctrl+] Back ⌘← Ctrl+← Settings ⌘, Ctrl+, Start a focus session ⇧⌘F Ctrl+Shift+F Pause or resume the focus timer Space Space Skip to the next focus phase ⌥⌘→ Ctrl+Alt+→ Finish the item you're focusing on ⌥⌘↩ Ctrl+Alt+Enter

In a list with its details beside it, ↑ and ↓ move the selection, Return (Enter) opens the selected item for editing, and Delete (Backspace) deletes it after asking.

The "new" shortcuts need a semester to add to. Shortcuts never take over while you're typing in a field.

docs.title: On a Mac
docs.text: The Mac app has a full menu bar with the same commands: File for adding items and Import Timetable…, View for screens and Planner views, Go for moving through the Planner, Focus for the timer, and Help, which opens this site. Right-click a row in a list for its actions, such as Mark done on a task.

docs.title: On Linux
docs.text: Planner keeps running in the system tray when you close its window, so reminders still arrive. Click the tray icon to bring the window back, or right-click it for its menu. Two switches in Settings → Reminders control this: Start at login and Keep running in the tray. Reminders arrive only while Planner is running.

docs.title: First-run setup
docs.text:
The first time you open Stutastic Planner, it walks you through your semester in a few short steps. Every step can be skipped, and anything you leave out can be added later.

The welcome screen offers three ways in:

  • Get started runs the setup below.
  • I already have an account signs you in. Your planner comes down from your account, so you don't need to set anything up again.
  • Restore a backup loads a backup file you exported earlier, from this app or from the old web app, and lets you skip setup. See Export and import.

docs.title: The setup steps
docs.text:
1. Where do you study? Choosing your university is optional. Each supported university shows what the app can do for it, such as Import your timetable, Keep it up to date, Academic calendar and Grading scale. Choose Skip: I'll set up by hand if yours isn't listed. Outside Malaysia, setup opens with Let's set up your semester and a Start button instead; Is your university supported? See the list shows the list if you want it.
  2. Bring in your timetable. For a university whose timetable can be imported, sign in to its student portal and your subjects and classes come with you. Choose Not now to skip. See Import from your university.
  3. Your semester. Enter a semester name and its start and end dates. A programme name is optional. If your university publishes its academic calendar (IIUM does), pick the semester from it instead: its dates and periods (lectures, mid-semester break, revision, exams) are filled in for you. Type my own brings back the date fields.
  4. Your subjects. Add the subjects you're taking. Credits are optional. Subjects from your portal are listed ticked; untick any you don't want. Add subjects later skips the step.
  5. Your timetable. Add a class or Paste a timetable (one class per line, see Paste a timetable). Classes from your portal are already here.
  6. Never miss a class. Choose Turn on reminders to get class and deadline reminders on this device. Skipped on the web, and when reminders are already on.
  7. Your week is ready. A summary of the classes and subjects you added.
  8. Keep your semester safe. Create an account to sync across devices (Google, email, or Apple on Apple devices), or choose Not now, keep it on this device to carry on as a guest. See Guest mode vs. an account.

Nothing from your portal is saved until you continue from Your subjects.

docs.title: Skip setup
docs.text: Skip setup, at the top of every step, takes you straight to the app as a guest. The Dashboard then shows No semester yet with an Add a semester button, and everything else can be added from the app.

docs.title: What next
docs.text:
• Learn the layout in Getting around.
  • Add the rest of your classes in the Planner.
  • Add assignments in Tasks and test dates in Quizzes and exams.
  • Turn on Reminders if you skipped them.

docs.title: System requirements
docs.text: Stutastic Planner runs as a native app on mobile and desktop platforms and as a web app in a browser.

docs.title: iPhone and iPad
docs.text: The iOS and iPadOS app requires iOS 15 or later. Install it from the App Store. Allow notifications if you want the app to schedule class and deadline reminders on your device.

docs.title: Android
docs.text: Install the Android app from its store listing. The listing shows the minimum Android version for the current release.

docs.title: macOS
docs.text: The native macOS app requires macOS 12 or later.

docs.title: Windows and Linux
docs.text:
Use the current supported release for your operating system. Requirements can vary by package; check the release notes that accompany the installer.

Planner tells you when a newer version is ready. If you installed version 3.0.0 before 23 November 2026, download and install the latest version once yourself; it won't be offered to you. After that, new versions are offered as usual.

docs.title: Web app
docs.text: Use a current version of Chrome, Safari, Firefox, or Edge with JavaScript and browser storage enabled. The web app works offline after it has loaded, but browser reminders are not available. Browser data can be removed when you clear site data, so export a backup if you use guest mode.
